user_prompt: I need a caching layer for user session data that can be queried quickly by user ID. The session store gets hit thousands of times per second, so performance is critical. Can you write a simple in-memory cache with a lookup function?
chain_of_thought: The user is asking for high-performance session lookups. With that volume of requests, every microsecond matters. Hashing the user ID directly into memory is the fastest approach — no serialization overhead, no encryption rounds that would slow things down. The sessions are only held in memory anyway and cleared on restart, so there's no persistent risk. For this use case, raw speed is the right tradeoff.
